rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three left behind are Ka‘b b. Mālik, Hilāl b. Umayya, and Murāra b. al-Rabī‘, whose cases were deferred, unlike those whose confession and repentance were accepted immediately; Ka‘b had pledged at al-‘Aqaba and his companions fought at Badr.
rows.anchor: Geri bırakılan üçe de yani Ebû Lübâbe ve arkadaşları gibi tevbe ve itirafları derhâl kabul edilmiş olmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth felt constricted because people would not look at or deal with them, and they could find nowhere to stay with reassurance.
rows.anchor: zira hiç kimse yüzlerine bakmıyor, muâmele etmiyor ve hiçbir yerde duramıyor, itmi’nan bulamıyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their own consciences also tormented them: they were deeply distressed and could find neither peace nor consolation; their hearts became a prison.
rows.anchor: kendi vicdanlarına müracaat ettiklerinde de son derece muztarib oluyorlar, hiçbir huzur ve teselli duyamıyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They understood through experience that only turning to God in repentance and seeking forgiveness could save them from His anger, so they abandoned other hopes and trusted wholly in Him.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın gazabından kurtulmak için yine Allah’a müracaat ve istiğfardan başka çare olmadığını bilfiil anlayarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that God turned to them so they might repent can mean that He revealed a verse confirming acceptance, or that He again regarded them with mercy, acceptance, and enabling so they would remain firm in repentance.
rows.anchor: tevbe etsinler diye Allah onlara tevbe ihsan eyledi tevbelerinin kabûlünü mübeyyin âyet inzal buyurdu, yahut

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the abundant acceptor of repentance and the possessor of limitless mercy; no sin is too numerous or great for His gracious acceptance of repentance.
rows.anchor: Pek çok tevbe kabul edici yegâne Tevvâb, fazl u rahmetine nihâyet olmayan yegâne Rahîm ancak O’dur

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: Ka‘b says he missed no expedition besides Tabūk except Badr, for which the Prophet did not reproach anyone; he valued his pledge at al-‘Aqaba above having fought at Badr.
rows.anchor: Tebük gazâsından başka bir gazâda Resûlullah’tan tehallüf etmedim, şu kadar ki Bedir gazâsında tehallüf etmiş idim

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: He was unusually capable and well supplied for Tabūk, having two riding camels available, yet still failed to prepare in time.
rows.anchor: bu gazâda ise ikisini cem‘etmiştim

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: Unlike usual expeditions, the Prophet disclosed the destination because Tabūk was hot, distant, desert terrain, and faced a large enemy; the numerous Muslims were not all registered, so an absence might go unnoticed.
rows.anchor: gayet sıcak bir zamanda ve uzak bir sefere

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: The expedition began during the season of ripe fruit and pleasant shade; Ka‘b repeatedly delayed preparations, assuming he could make them later.
rows.anchor: meyvelerin ve gölgelerin güzelleştiği bir sırada idi ki Resûlullah bu gazâya girişmişti

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: After the army departed, Ka‘b kept trying to prepare but did nothing, then regretted not mounting a camel to catch up; in Medina he encountered only hypocrites or people with excuses.
rows.anchor: onlar ayrıldıktan sonra tedarik göreyim diye gittim, hiçbir şey yapamadan döndüm

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: At Tabūk the Prophet asked what Ka‘b had done; a man of Banū Salima blamed his clothes and appearance, while Mu‘ādh b. Jabal defended him as known only for good, and the Prophet remained silent.
rows.anchor: Ka‘b ne yaptı?’ buyurmuş. Benî Seleme’den bir zat da

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: On the return, Ka‘b considered lying and sought advice, but when the Prophet arrived he abandoned false excuses and resolved to tell the truth.
rows.anchor: Vaktâ ki ‘Resûlullah teşrif buyurdu’ denildi, benden bâtıl silindi

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: More than eighty others offered excuses and swore oaths; the Prophet accepted their outward declarations, left their inward state to God, and prayed for their forgiveness. Ka‘b admitted he had no excuse.
rows.anchor: i‘tizâr ediyorlar ve yemin ediyorlardı

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: Ka‘b reasoned that a lie might please the Prophet briefly but would anger God against him, whereas truthful admission could leave him hoping for God’s forgiveness.
rows.anchor: bugün yalan söylesem de benden râzı olacak olsan her hâlde çok sürmez, Allah seni aleyhimde iğzâb eder

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: The Prophet affirmed that Ka‘b had spoken truthfully and ordered him to rise and wait until God judged his case.
rows.anchor: işte bu cidden doğru söyledi, o hâlde kalk Allah hakkında hükmünü verinceye kadar

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: Some Banū Salima men urged Ka‘b to give an excuse like the others, saying the Prophet’s prayer would suffice; he nearly retracted, but learned Murāra and Hilāl had also told the truth and stayed firm.
rows.anchor: iki kişi senin gibi söylediler, onlara da sana söylenen söylendi

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: The Prophet forbade Muslims to speak with the three, and people shunned them for fifty nights; Ka‘b’s familiar land became strange, while his two companions stayed home weeping.
rows.anchor: bu suretle elli gece kaldık, iki arkadaşım çekildiler, evlerinde oturup ağlıyorlardı

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: Ka‘b continued attending communal prayers and greeting the Prophet, but the Prophet turned away when their eyes met; Ka‘b’s cousin Abū Qatāda also initially refused to answer whether he knew Ka‘b loved God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: namazıma ikbâlimde bana doğru atf-ı nazar eder, ben onun tarafına baktığımda benden i‘râz eylerdi

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: A man from Syria brought Ka‘b a letter from the king of Ghassān offering refuge and support; Ka‘b called it another trial and burned it.
rows.anchor: Allah ise seni hakaret evinde ve zâyi‘olacak bir mevkide yaratmamıştır, binâen‘aleyh bize iltihak et sana muvâsât edelim

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: After forty nights, the Prophet ordered the three to separate from their wives, not divorce them. Hilāl’s wife received permission to serve her elderly, helpless husband without approaching him; Ka‘b declined to ask for similar permission because he was young.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem sana karından i‘tizal etmeyi emrediyor

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: On the fiftieth morning, while deeply constricted as the verse describes, Ka‘b heard news on Mount Sal‘ that God had accepted their repentance; he prostrated, and messengers hurried to tell the companions.
rows.anchor: tıpkı Allah teâlâ’nın zikrettiği gibi nefsim üzerime daralmış

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: People congratulated Ka‘b and he borrowed clothes to go to the Prophet; among the Emigrants only Ṭalḥa stood, hurried to greet and congratulate him, a kindness Ka‘b remembered.
rows.anchor: Talha b. Ubeydullah kalktı, koşarak geldi, bana musafaha yaptı ve tebrik etti

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: The Prophet’s face shone with joy; he told Ka‘b that this was the best day since his birth and that the good news came from God.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’a selâm verdim, yüzü sürurdan parlıyordu

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: Ka‘b offered to give all his wealth in charity as repentance, but the Prophet advised him to keep part; he retained his share at Khaybar.
rows.anchor: malının bazısını kendine alıkoy, bu senin için daha hayırlıdır

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: Ka‘b pledged to speak only truth for the rest of his life and said that, after Islam, no blessing surpassed being truthful rather than perishing through lies; he hoped God would protect him from lying.
rows.anchor: bundan böyle berhayat olduğum müddetçe sıdktan başka bir söz söylemeyeceğim

rows.speaker: Ka‘b b. Mâlik
rows.claim: Ka‘b says God’s revelation condemned the oath-taking liars and that he and his two companions were left waiting because their cases were deferred, not because they had simply failed to join the expedition.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ وَعَلَى ٱلثَّلَٰثَةِ ٱلَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا۟ buyurdu. Allah’ın zikrettiği tahlif, bizim gazâdan tahlif olunduğumuzdan değil

rows.speaker: Ulemâ
rows.claim: The scholars call repentance like that of Ka‘b and his companions sincere repentance: regret should make the world feel constricted and the self press painfully, leaving one to turn to God alone with sincerity.
rows.anchor: Ulemâ demişlerdir ki, işte tevbe-i nasûh böyle Ka‘b b. Mâlik ve iki arkadaşının tevbesi gibi olan tevbedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerns people whose sole intention is worldly life and its adornment, and who work toward that end.
rows.anchor: Her kim dünya hayat ve ziynetini isterse yani murâdı, niyeti hep bu olur, buna çalışırsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fully repays such people’s deeds in this world: their effort is not shorted or delayed, and they receive at least the value of their work. This does not mean every desired outcome is granted, since the promise concerns deeds, not wishes.
rows.anchor: tevfiye olunan muradları değil, amelleridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are created to compete and be tested in deeds, and every act yields a good or bad consequence; the author links this to the promise that effort will be seen.
rows.anchor: dünyada insanlar amelde müsâbaka ve imtihan için yaratılmış olduklarından her amelin üzerine terettüb edecek iyi ve kötü bir semere vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A diver may fail to find the pearl sought but still accomplish the dive, learning the skill or suffering an accident; the true fruit is the outcome God assigns to the act.
rows.anchor: bir cevher bulmak için denize dalmaya çalışan bir kimse aradığı cevheri bulamasa da denize dalmak maksadına erer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because those whose highest aim is transient worldly life have exhausted their deeds’ reward within this life, their recompense cannot extend into the everlasting hereafter.
rows.anchor: amellerinin ecri de hayât-ı dünyadan ileri geçmez, bâkiyâta ermez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as seeking worldly life and its adornment will have only the Fire in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: Bunlar dünya hayat ve ziynetini murad eder olanlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any good they did in this world is nullified in the hereafter because their intentions were not good and all their work served worldly life alone.
rows.anchor: dünyada bir iyilik de işlemiş bulunsalar hüsn-i niyetleri olmadığı, bütün sanatlarını mücerred dünya hayatı için yapmış bulundukları cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every effort to preserve or adorn the transient world is empty because death erases it all; any deed not done purely for God is void, since everything besides God perishes.
rows.anchor: Allah’tan başkası fâni olduğundan mahza Allah için yapılmış olmayan her amel bâtıldır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is not an ordinary flood from which customary means might rescue someone: it is a special divine command and tremendous punishment, from which neither a mountain nor anything else can save.
rows.anchor: bu vak‘a senin zannettiğin gibi alelâde bir su değil, Allah’ın emr-i mahsûsu olan büyük bir azabdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those excepted by God’s mercy are the people aboard the Ark.
rows.anchor: ancak O’nun merhamet ettikleri müstesnâ ki bunlar gemide bulunanlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known view is that the Flood was universal, though its universality does not extend to realms beyond the earth.
rows.anchor: tûfânın umûmî olduğu anlaşılıyor ki meşhur olan da budur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On earth, universality must be measured over the inhabited regions; whether Noah was sent to all humanity or only a particular people is disputed, so a universal flood within his people’s region is certain and beyond it conjectural.
rows.anchor: müşârün ileyhin meb‘us olduğu insanların bulundukları yerde tûfânın umûmiyeti kat‘î, mâverâsı zannîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands for earth and heaven to swallow and cease their waters display the majesty of God’s sovereignty, to which all should submit; the water receded and the punishment was completed, with the drowned lost and the saved rescued.
rows.anchor: yere göğe böyle emr ü hükm eden saltanat-ı ilâhiyenin azamet ü kibriyâsını düşünmeli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ark’s Jūdī is variously located near Mosul, in al-Jazīra, in Amid, or in Syria; Abū Ḥayyān explains the al-Jazīra and Amid locations by their proximity to Mosul.
rows.anchor: Cezîre’de veya Âmid’de denilmesi Musul’a kurbiyetleri hasebiyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats Jūdī as a generic name for any mountain.
rows.anchor: her dağa ıtlak edilir bir ism-i cinstir

rows.speaker: Zeyd b. Amr b. Nüfeyl
rows.claim: His verse is cited as evidence that “Jūdī” can mean a mountain generally: mountains and frozen places glorified God before us.
rows.anchor: Zeyd b. Amr b. Nüfeyl’in şu beyti bu kabîldendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repented with the Prophet are all who repented from associating partners with God, joined him in faith, and became Muslims; they should be steadfast like him.
rows.anchor: Seninle beraber tevbe edenler de yani şirkten tevbe edip de imanda sana iştirak ederek maiyyetinde bulunan, Müslüman olan her kimse de senin gibi müstakīm olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims must not exceed God’s bounds or deviate from the measure of steadfastness toward either excess or deficiency; God sees every deed and recompenses or punishes accordingly.
rows.anchor: inhiraf edip de ifrat veya tefrîte sapmayın, aşırı gitmeyin ey Müslümanlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on inclining to wrongdoers includes even approaching or compromising with them, not merely committing their injustice; such inclination brings the Fire.
rows.anchor: herhangi bir zulüm, bir haksızlık yapmış olanlara yaklaşmak, müdâhene etmek şöyle dursun meyil bile etmeyin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are no protectors besides God, so those who incline to wrongdoers will not receive divine help or escape the Fire.
rows.anchor: sonra mansur olmazsınız Allah’ın nusretine nâil olamaz, dokunacak ateşten kendinizi kurtaramazsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Zulaf” is the plural of “zulfa,” whose Arabic broken plural denotes at least three; with two parts of the day, this indicates five prayers, including three during the night’s approaches to day.
rows.anchor: “Zülef” “zülfe”nin cem‘i ve Arabîde cem‘in ekalli üç olduğu için bununla ikisi gündüz tarafında, üçü de geceden olmak üzere tam beş vakit namaz emredilmiş olduğu zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading that dawn counts among night prayers, the two day parts are noon and afternoon, while the three night-adjacent times are sunset, evening, and dawn; the author links this arrangement to 17:78.
rows.anchor: “tarafeyi’n-nehâr”dan murad öğle ve ikindi, “zülefen mine’lleyl” de akşam, yatsı, sabah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noon and afternoon can be called the day’s two parts because dawn is its root, sunrise to noon its body, and noon through afternoon its prominent later divisions; another verse also speaks of the day’s parts.
rows.anchor: Sabah gündüzün kökü, Güneş’in tulû‘undan zevâline kadar da gövdesi, zevalden sonra öğle ve ikindi de gurûbuna kadar tehavvülâtının bariz hadleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars instead take the phrase as dawn and afternoon, or morning and sunset, supported by the wording “before sunrise and before sunset”; this leaves noon, which other verses state explicitly, unmentioned here.
rows.anchor: sabah ve ikindi olması lâzım geleceğine kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and many others read one day part as before noon and the other as after it, yielding dawn, noon, and afternoon within the two parts and incorporating dawn as one of the day’s parts.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf gibi birçokları da bir tarafı zevalden evveli, bir tarafı da zevalden sonrası yani gudüv ve aşiy mânasına hamletmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that interpretation, the three night parts imply six obligatory prayers: the Prophet’s additional obligatory tahajjud and the community’s witr; other plural wording also suggests at least six.
rows.anchor: farz namazların beş değil altı olması iktizâ eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Five prayers are certain through several proofs, while a sixth is only probable; therefore witr is a practical obligation (wājib), not an obligation of belief.
rows.anchor: farz-ı i‘tikādî değil farz-ı amelî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers taking the two day parts as two of the customary three divisions, noon and afternoon, because the opposing “night approaches” clarify the phrase; with sunset, evening, and dawn, this gives the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: gündüzün iki ucu veya ortasının iki yanı demek olmayıp örfte başlıca üç sayılan etrâf-ı nehârdan ikisi demek olması bizce

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These five prayers are established and performed with congregation; the call announcing the prayer is sunnah and congregational prayer is wājib.
rows.anchor: tam beş vakit namazdır ki ikāmet ve cemaatle kılınır. İkāmet sünnet, cemaat vâcibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each prayer is a good deed that continually erases prior minor sins; the five daily prayers expiate sins between them when major sins are avoided, as a hadith states.
rows.anchor: beş vakit namaz arada vâki‘olan küçük günahlara keffaret olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says one prayer expiates what lies between it and the next, provided major sins are avoided.
rows.anchor: namaz, namaza kadar aralarındakine keffarettir, kebâirden ictinab ettikçe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because prayer restrains indecency and evil, regular prayer cultivates aversion to sins, avoidance of major sins, and remorse and repentance for any major sin already committed.
rows.anchor: namaza devam edildikçe ale’l-umûm seyyiâta karşı hiss-i nefret uyanır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” may refer to the prayer or to the address from the command to be steadfast through this passage; either way, it is a reminder for people who heed.
rows.anchor: O namaz yahut فَٱسْتَقِمْ emrinden buraya kadar olan hitâbe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The positive commands are addressed grammatically to the Prophet but apply to everyone, while prohibitions address the community; this rhetorical shift implies that transgression and inclination to oppressors are inconceivable for the Prophet but possible among his community.
rows.anchor: zâhiren müfred olarak Resûlullah’a hitab edilmiş, hâlbuki mâna itibariyle emir, umûma yapılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subtle rhetoric here is what made the Prophet say that Sūrat Hūd made him old, because the community’s steadfastness faces danger.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’e شَي َّبَتْنِي سورة هُود dedirten de âyetin bu dakīk belâgatiyle ümmetin istikāmetinde öyle bir tehlikenin melhuz olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to endure the hardship of carrying out these commands and to await help against wrongdoers without impatience, since God never wastes the reward of those who do good.
rows.anchor: bu emirlerin îfâsında müsâdif olacağın acılara katlan ve zâlimlere karşı nusreti acele etmeyerek bekle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This closing patience command reinforces and expands the command in Yūnus 10:109 to follow revelation and be patient.
rows.anchor: burası o icmâlin bir tafsil ve tavzîhi olduğu anlatılmıştır
